title: Bound root-mutation cost by something that does not grow with closed history (for example an incremental state checksum)
outcome: When the council's revisit trigger is met, decide and file a concrete design whose root-mutation work does not grow with closed history, with the storage and conversion consequences named. Do not activate on the basis of this filing alone.
acceptance: The revisit trigger is recorded from evidence: a live root passes 1.5 times the post-fix problem point recorded by the constant-factor follow-up, or an Engram or TermAl agent reports a mutation over its applicable budget.

A council-reviewed design identifies how mutation work is bounded independently of closed history, including correctness, concurrency, replay and audit consequences, with independently checkable structural validation proposed.
Any durable checksum or stored-format change has its explicit import conversion and every-live-store migration consequence named, and Greg's recorded format decision precedes any stored change.
